_doc: Rules of the PowerShell extractor (graph.extract.pwsh; the `protocol` key is read as in ts_generic.rules_of, names are case-folded). A property of a class is a data member: a hashtable cast ([Foo]@{Name = 'x'}), New-Object -Property, ConvertFrom-Json and Select-Object name it by a string, no member access shows the use; it lives with its class. So do the methods the language calls by convention: ToString, Equals, GetHashCode, CompareTo, Dispose, GetEnumerator, Parse (a string cast to the type), Clone. A class-based DSC resource has Get, Set and Test methods that the Local Configuration Manager calls: they live with the class too (a plain class with such a method keeps it alive, never a false dead). sinks: a string handed to a command or a member that EVALUATES it is code. mode command = the string is a script (Invoke-Expression, ScriptBlock::Create, InvokeScript, AddScript): the first word of every statement is a command, a call; mode words = the string is a command line of a launcher (pwsh -Command, Start-Process -ArgumentList): every word that is no parameter is a weak ref, a path is an exec. A word with a variable in it is a name glob (`Do-$action` -> name:do-*); a computed argument of a command-mode sink is a dyn site. Keys are lowercase, `.exe` dropped; members are `owner.name` (`?` = a receiver the text does not name). globs: Get-ChildItem and its aliases enumerate the files a loop dot-sources (the classic module layout `foreach ($f in @($public + $private)) { . $f.FullName }`): when the file loads a computed path, the pattern of the enumeration (path / filter / recurse parameters, switch parameters take no value; helpers are commands that only build the path) is an include glob. get-command: a string with a wildcard names functions by pattern (`Get-Command 'Test-*'`). script_skip: commands at the top level that a library file runs too (strict mode, module loading, aliases, type data): they do not make the file a script.
